text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE

- A study by Albania's Consumer Association said in a report that Coca Cola Bottling Enterprise Tirana uses expiry dates on its drinks that are too long and claims there is less liquid in the bottles than required.
- Austria's OMV oil company wants another offshore concession from the Albanian government after its first offshore drilling failed to strike oil.
- A group of 17 monitors from the Council of Europe assigned to observe local elections next Sunday has arrived in Albania.
- The father of a youngster who threatened to detonate a bomb if he was not allowed to meet President Sali Berisha in April says his son is mentally deranged.
- Americans have adopted more Albanian children than children from other countries, says the head of Albania's Adoption Commission.

- Albania's Helsinki Committee branch wants the alleged beating of a citizen by a police squad to be fully investigated. The man is still in a coma after the beating which came after he denied he was driving too fast.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Italian police have arrested nine Albanians and one Italian after they found 100 kg of marijuana in their cars.
- Italian authorities sent home 50 Albanians who had entered Italy without papers.

- A delegation of the Organisation for Cooperation and Security in Europe is still waiting for an official answer from the Albanian government to have a group of 60 observers monitor next Sunday's local polls.
- About 96 percent of the population has been vaccinated against polio, which has killed 12 people since April.
- A money-dealer in the central town of Elbasan has been kidnapped by two youngster who asked him to exchange a million drachmas for them.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- Albanian President Sali Berisha, campaigning for his ruling Democratic Party candidates in Sunday's local polls, tells voters Democrat candidates would have the support of the central government.
ZERI I POPULLIT

- Jailed Socialist leader Fatos Nano tells the paper in an interview that the opposition does not spurn the achievements of post-communist reform but wants to make a distinction between real reform and other changes masquerading as reform.
ALBANIA
- Police have uncovered a guerrilla organisation whose aim was to overthrow the government and which ordered the killing of the general director of prisons.
